summary: Ryushin Sudo was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Taisho University. He later served as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Ryushin Uryuzu studied at Ryukoku University from circa 1951 to 1955. His career included posts at the Tibetan Tripitaka Research Institute (attested 1962) and as professor at Kyoto Women's University (attested 1982).

Ryusho Hikata specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying under Junjiro Takakusu at the University of Tokyo and receiving a doctorate from Tohoku University. He held professorships and a deanship at Kyushu University, and served as president of Fukuoka Women's University.

Ryuta Kikutani works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He has held appointments as a special researcher at Tohoku University (attested 2015), at Kyoto University's Hakubi Center (attested 2020), and as an associate professor at Koyasan University (attested 2026).

Indologist Ryutaro Tsuchida studied at the University of Tokyo and completed his doctoral work at the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau and others. He served as an assistant at Marburg before becoming professor and later professor emeritus at the University of Tokyo.

Takayoku Kimura, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Komazawa University. He worked as a research assistant at the University of Tokyo (c. 1973–1978), lecturer at Yamaguchi University (attested 1996), and head priest at Kaichō-ji (attested 2003).
Ryuzan Nishimoto was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Chishu Kitagawa and traditional teacher Chijo Kitagawa in 1916.
Ryōkei Kaginushi was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor in the Faculty of Letters and university professor at Otani University, attested in 1978 and 1993.
Ryōmin Akizuki worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo, taught Makio Takemura, and held a post at Saitama Medical University.

Rüdiger Schmitt specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied under Karl Hoffmann from circa 1960 to 1965 and held a position at Saarland University from circa 1979 to 2004.

S. Kuppuswami Sastri was an Indologist and philosopher educated at St. Peter's College and the University of Madras. He served as principal of Madras Sanskrit College and Rajah's College, and held professorships at Presidency College and Annamalai University.

S. M. Natesa Sastri was an Indologist educated at Government Arts College, Kumbakonam, and the University of Madras. From circa 1883 to 1888, he served as an assistant to Robert Sewell at the Archaeological Survey of India.

S. N. Balagangadhara works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at National College, Bangalore, and earned his doctorate at Ghent University under Etienne Vermeersch, later serving as director at Ghent University and co-chair at the American Academy of Religion.
S. N. Krishna is an Indology scholar who studied for a Ph.D. at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor T. V. Vasudeva, attested in 2026.
S. N. Savadi was an Indologist who held posts at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1953 and 1969.

S. S. Misra worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as professor and head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Lucknow (attested 1958) and as professor of Indology and linguistics at Banaras Hindu University.

S. S. Suryanarayana Sastri was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. At the University of Madras, he held posts as reader in Indian philosophy (attested 1929) and reader and head of the Department of Philosophy (attested 1942).

S. Sankaranarayanan was an Indologist and historian who served as an honorary professor at the Adyar Library and Research Centre from circa 1986 to 1999, and held a post at the Chinmaya International Foundation in 1999.

S. Srikanta Sastri was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore, under M. H. Krishna. He later served on the faculty at the University of Mysore from circa 1939 to 1966.

Saba Mahmood was a scholar of religious studies and anthropology who studied at the University of Washington and Stanford University. She held posts at the University of Chicago (c. 1999–2004) and as professor of sociocultural anthropology at UC Berkeley (2004–2018).
